tips:
**Denominal Verbs** (verbs from nouns):

Hebrew productively creates new verbs by taking a noun and placing its consonants into a verb pattern, usually **Pi'el**.

**Technology verbs (all Pi'el):**

| Noun | Verb | Meaning |
|------|------|---------|
| טֶלֶפוֹן (telephone) | טִלְפֵּן | to call/phone |
| גּוּגְל (Google) | גִּיגֵּל | to google |
| תּוֹכְנָה (software) | תִּכְנֵת | to program |
| מֵייל (email) | מִיילֵל | to email |
| סֶמֶס (SMS) | סִימֵס | to text |
| פַקְס (fax) | פִיקְסֵס | to fax |

**Action verbs from nouns:**

| Noun | Verb | Meaning |
|------|------|---------|
| מַפָּה (map) | מִיפָּה | to map |
| אוֹת (sign/signal) | אוֹתֵת | to signal |
| מִסְגֶרֶת (frame) | מִיסְגֵר | to frame |
| דֶלֶק (fuel) | תִּדְלֵק | to fuel/refuel |
| חִיסּוּן (vaccine) | חִיסֵּן | to vaccinate |
| בֹּרֶג (screw) | הִבְרִיג | to screw in (Hif'il!) |
| מַחְשֵׁב (computer) | מִיחְשֵׁב | to computerize |

**Note:** Most denominal verbs use **Pi'el**, but some use **Hif'il** (הִבְרִיג from בֹּרֶג). This is a very productive process in modern Hebrew - whenever a new technology noun enters the language, a verb often follows!
